senses.sense_definition: The act of correcting something that is wrong or adjusting it to be right.

examples.text: The <w>rectification</w> of the error in the financial report was completed by the accounting team.
He sought the <w>rectification</w> of his past mistakes through honest work and dedication.

senses.sense_definition: The process of purifying a substance by repeated distillation.

examples.text: The <w>rectification</w> of the alcohol ensures it reaches the required level of purity for laboratory use.
Continuous <w>rectification</w> is essential in the production of high-grade chemical solvents.

senses.sense_definition: The mathematical process of finding the length of a curve by determining a straight line of equal length.

examples.text: The <w>rectification</w> of a complex curve often requires advanced calculus techniques.
Students studied the <w>rectification</w> of arcs to understand the relationship between curves and lines.

senses.sense_definition: The geometric process of truncating a polyhedron by replacing vertices with faces at the midpoints of edges.

examples.text: The <w>rectification</w> of an icosahedron results in a new geometric solid.
In geometry, the <w>rectification</w> of a polytope creates a shape with new faces at each vertex.

senses.sense_definition: The act of setting up a globe correctly to solve a specific geographical problem.

The <w>rectification</w> of the globe allows for accurate measurement of distances and angles.

Scholars analyze the <w>rectification</w> campaigns to understand the consolidation of political power.

senses.sense_definition: The process of determining an accurate birth time for an individual using significant life events.

examples.text: Astrologers perform <w>rectification</w> when the exact time of birth is unknown.
The <w>rectification</w> of the birth chart relies on matching past life events to planetary positions.
